title: Shepherd of Souls, with Pitying Eye
description: Shepherd of Souls, with Pitying Eye in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 82. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Shep-herd of souls, with pity-ing eye The thou-sands of our Is-rael see: To thee in their be-half we cry, Our-selves but new-ly found in thee.

lines: Shepherd of souls, with pitying eye
The thousands of our Israel see:
To thee in their behalf we cry,
Ourselves but newly found in thee.
See where o'er desert wastes they err,
And neither food nor feeder have,
Nor fold, nor place of refuge near,
For no man cares their souls to save.
Wild as the ill-taught Indian's brood
The Christian savages remain;
Strangers, yea, enemies to God,
They make thee spill thy blood in vain.
Thy people, Lord, are sold for nought,
Nor know they their Redeemer nigh;
They perish, whom thyself hast bought,
Their souls for lack of knowledge die.
The pit its mouth hath opened wide,
To swallow up its careless prey:
Why should they die, when thou hast died,
Hast died to bear their sins away?
Why should the foe thy purchase seize?
Remember, Lord, thy dying groans:
The meed of all thy sufferings these,
O claim them for thy ransomed ones!
Extend to these thy pardoning grace,
To these be thy salvation showed:
O add them to thy chosen race!
O sprinkle all their hearts with blood!
Still let the publicans draw near:
Open the door of faith and heaven,
And grant their hearts thy word to hear,
And witness all their sins forgiven.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
